questions.question: When a ball is thrown upward, its total energy:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Remains same**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

 
• When a ball is thrown upward, its total energy **remains the same.**
 
• When an object is thrown vertically upwards, its **potential energy keeps on increasing** and kinetic energy keeps on decreasing.
 
• The total energy of the ball remains the same.
 
• At maximum height, the velocity is zero (no kinetic energy) and the ball will have only potential energy.
 
• The energy possessed by a body by virtue of its position is called **potential energy.**
 
• The energy possessed by a body due to its motion is called **kinetic energy.**
 
• Kinetic energy is always **positive.**
 
• Energy may be transformed from one form to another but the total energy of an isolated system remains constant.
 
• When an object is thrown vertically upwards then **energy conversion takes place, **energy can neither be created nor destroyed**.**

__
 
• **Impedance** is the total sum of** resistance and reactance.**
 
• The **SI Unit **of **Impedance(Z), resistance(R)**, and **reactance(X) **is **Ohm(Ω).**
 
• **Reactance **is a **kind of imaginary resistance **offered by electrical components like **Capacitance and Inductor.**
 
 
• Reactance offered by the Inductor is called **Inductive reactance**, given as **XL = 2πfL**.
 
• Reactance offered by the Capacitor is called **Capacitor reactance**, given as ** XC=(1)/(2pi fC).**
 
• Where 'f' - frequency of the source, 'L' - Inductance, and 'C' - Capacitance.

questions.question: Which of the following bonds are weakest in nature?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Hydrogen bond.**__

__**Concept:**__

**Chemical bond:**

__
 
• A chemical bond is a force or **linkage **which holds two or more atoms together in a stable molecule.
 
• The driving force for atoms to combine is related to their tendency to attain stable electronic configuration.
 
• A chemical bond may be formed either by electron transfer or electron sharing.
 
• 
 
Ionic Bonds:

 
 
• 
 
​Ionic bond formation occurs via electrostatic attraction between two ions.

 
 
• One ion is positively charged and the other is negatively charged like in** NaCl.​**
 
 
 
• Covalent bonds:
 
 
• Covalent bond formation occurs when there is electron sharing occurs between two atoms.
 
• The electron pair is shared equally between the atoms forming the bond-like in Cl2.
 
• When there exists a single bond between two atoms, there is only a sigma bond.
 
• When there exist multiple bonds between atoms, there is only one sigma bond and others are pi bond.
 
 

​Explanation:__

 
• Whether a bond is weak or strong depends on the **extent of linkage or interaction **among the molecules or atoms.
 
• Besides the chemical bond, there exist** interactions between** the** molecules**, which are not actual bonds, which means that** there is no sharing or transfer of electrons** but only** interaction** between the molecules is there.
 
• The types of interactions are:
 
 
• **Electrostatic:** They are interactions between charged molecules.
 
• **Induction:** These types of interactions arise when there is induction of dipole in the molecule.
 
• **Dispersion:** These are also called London forces or Van der Waals forces and exists mostly in covalent molecules.
 
• **Hydrogen bonds:** Hydrogen bonds are the** dipole-dipole interactions** that occur when a **Hydrogen** is bonded to a very **electronegative atom** like oxygen, Nitrogen. It is not a covalent bond.
 
 
 
• So, the **Hydrogen bond **is just an **interaction **between the **Hydrogen** and an **electronegative element** where there is** no electron exchange **leading to weak bonding between molecules** whereas **a **single bond, double bond, and triple bond** are** covalent bonds** and not just interactions.
 
• **Chemical bonds are much much stronger than chemical interactions**.
 
• It is difficult to break chemical bonds whereas Hydrogen bonds are easily and rapidly formed and broken under normal biological conditions.
 
• Hence, the** bond strength **order is: 

**triple bond > double bond > single bond > H-Bond.**

Hence, the weakest among the bonds is the **Hydrogen bond.**

questions.question: Heavy water is mostly used in which of the following?

options.text: In both Nuclear reactors and Fire extinguisher

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is__** In nuclear reactors.**__

__**Explanation:**__

Heavy Water:__​__

 
• Deuterium oxide, D2O.
 
• It is an oxide of the isotope of hydrogen, Deuterium.
 
• It is a colourless and odourless liquid.
 
• A molecule of heavy water has two deuterium atoms in place of the two normal hydrogen atoms of ordinary "light" water.
 
• The presence of deuterium gives the water different nuclear properties, and the increase in mass gives it slightly different physical and chemical properties when compared to normal water.
 
• Heavy water is not radioactive.
 
• Heavy water is not safe to drink. 
 
• American scientist and Nobel laureate Harold Urey discovered the isotope deuterium in 1931.
 
• Argentina is the main producer of heavy water.
 
• Heavy water is used in certain types of nuclear reactors, where it acts as a neutron moderator to slow down neutrons so that they are more likely to react with the fissile uranium-235 than with uranium-238. ​

 
• Heavy water acts as a moderator when it is used in nuclear reactors.
 
• **Moderators are used to containing the velocity of neutrons used in the nuclear reactions so that they do not react with Uranium-238.**

questions.question: What type of wave is used in MRI machine?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Magnetic waves**__. 

__
 
• MRI scanners use strong magnetic fields, magnetic field gradients, and radio waves to generate images of the organs in the body. 
 
• MRI does not involve X-rays or the use of ionizing radiation, which distinguishes it from CT or CAT scans and PET scans.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

 
• MRI can be also known or called Magnetic Resonance imaging.
 
• In MRI the body is placed in a high strength magnetic field.
 
• This field is generated by a superconducting magnetic coil which is immersed in liquid helium.
 
• This field causes the alignment of the spins of the protons in the body of the patient.
 
• Pulses of radio waves are then used to excite the nuclei causing the alignment of the spins to undergo decoherence.
 
• When the spins realign, they release a radio signal which is picked up by antennae placed close to the body. 
 
• from this signal and by modulating the radio wave pulses different types of MR images are reconstructed.
 
• This is the basis of MR imaging.

questions.question: Two resistors, one of 10 Ω and the other of 20 Ω. are connected in series to a 6 V battery. The current in the circuit will be?
questions.solution:
As the Resistors are connected in series the equivalent resistance will be -

Rₑqv = R₁ + R₂

= 10 Ω + 20 Ω

= 30 Ω

According to Ohm’s law -

→ V = IR

→ I = V/R

→ I = 6/30 = 1/5 [V = 6 V given]

→ I = **__0.2 A__**

questions.question: Name the filtration units of the excretory system in human.
questions.solution:
__**Concept**__:

**Human Excretory system:**

__
 
• The system of the organ which is used to remove the waste product out from the body is called** the human excretory system**.
 
• The major waste product generated in the human body is urea, along with which some other toxins are also generated.
 
• Urea is eliminated by kidneys by the process of urination and solid wastes are removed from the body by the intestines.

**Excretory system organs:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e41f1740cdb8115a19d9bbfcf5e898af70219f2d79922d8483412abbbc330bb3.png] 

 
• **Kidneys:**It is a bean shaped organ. Its function is to clean blood and eliminate the waste from the blood in form of urine

 
• It is present in the abdomen, just below the diaphragm, and is protected by ribs.
 
• Each kidney weighs 120g to 170 g and 10-12 cm long and 5-7 cm wide and is the size of a fist.
 
• Kidneys are made up of subunits called Nephron

** **2.**Ureters: **​Each kidney is connected to the rinal pelvis by a thin muscular tube, this tube is called as **Ureter.**

 
• Its function is to propel urine from the kidney to the urinary Bladder from time to time.

 3**.Bladders:** It's the organ that controls the passage of urine, it is a muscular sac-like structure.

 
• The average capacity of the bladder is **400-600 ml.**
 
• It holds urine until its capacity expels, or till it gets full.

 4.**Urethra: **The Urethra is a tube made up of fibro muscular tissue that arises from the lower opening of the bladder, and open to the external uretral orifice.

 
• It helps to expel urine through the body, in the male it is also the tube that consist of the sperms.

**Explanation**__:

__
 
• In kidneys, the Nephron is the functional unit, each kidney has as many as 1 million nephrons in each human kidney.
 
• The basic functions of the **nephron** are to carry **out secretion** as well as the **process of excretion **and also called as** filtration unit of the human excretory system**.
 
• Each nephron is made up of a **Malpighian body.**
 
• **Nephrons** are of two types which are **Cortical Nephrons** and **Juxtamedullary Nephrons**.

**So, the Nephron is the part that is also called as filtration unit of the Excretory unit.__**

questions.question: The energy required to move a 60-coulomb charge through a potential difference of 1.5 V is
questions.solution:
__Concept:__

Potential difference or voltage (V) is given by

V = (W)/(Q)

Where,

W = Energy in joule

Q = Charge in coulomb

Also 1 joule / sec = 1 Watt

__Calculation:__

Potential difference = 1.5 V

Charge = 60 C

Energy required to move 60 C charge: 1.5 x 60 = 90 J

questions.question: Which gas is used in Soda Water?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The main ingredient in sweetened soft drinks is water; they are about 90 per cent carbonated water.
 
• Carbonated water is water that has been infused with carbon dioxide gas under pressure.
 
 
• This produces a bubbly drink that's also known as sparkling water, club soda, soda water, seltzer water, and fizzy water.
